text:
Samira K: Heads up: Veridian submitted a dispute for invoice VER-2026-310 ($6,400). Stripe dispute id dp_1Lz7Yq. Reason: 'unauthorized' charge. They want evidence within 7 days. @Priya can you take the lead?
Priya (Payments): On it. Which billing_project and API key? Need card last4 and email.
Samira K: Billing project veridian-prod, card last4 4246, email billing@veridian.example. Billed period 2026-07-02..2026-07-09.
Theo (CS): Customer says they never gave the keys to third parties and want immediate refund. They also requested we suspend billing until resolved.
Stripe-Bot: dispute.created id=dp_1Lz7Yq amount=6400 currency=USD reason=unauthorized created=1714501200
Ben C: Please pull request logs for that window: request_id, api_key_id, model, tokens, ip_address, response_code. Also need api_key creation event.
Priya (Payments): I'll compile the evidence: invoice PDF, usage CSV, key creation logs, support ticket thread, IP geo lookups, and any hold actions.
Theo (CS): I've sent the onboarding emails. They show user "clare.veridian@veridian.example" created a key on 2026-06-25 via the console. Attached link: https://cs.example/veridian/onboard-123 (internal).
Ben C: Quick log summary: usage concentrated on 2026-07-04 from api_key key_vdx77; 1.2M tokens, model rdx-14b, originating mostly from IP 18.197.12.9 and some calls from 185.62.9.10 (VPN). Response codes: 200 for 87%, 401 for 10% after key disabled, 403 none.
Samira K: Customer insists they didn't initiate this. Do we have any evidence of compromise (password resets, new sessions)?
Priya (Payments): Key creation came from corporate IP 18.197.12.9. No suspicious login or password reset around key creation. However, on 2026-07-03 at 03:12 UTC there are many calls from 185.62.9.10 which maps to a VPN provider.
OpsBot: Action logged: placed account veridian-prod into billing-review and disabled write keys at ts=1714504800 by Theo.
Samira K: Good. For the dispute bundle to Stripe we should: 1) provide usage CSV, 2) provide key lifecycle (created by which user, which IP), 3) support thread where customer denies authorization, 4) actions taken (hold + keys disabled), 5) any refunds/credits (none so far).
Ben C: I'll upload CSV and short timeline to ticket FT-3319. CSV link: https://support.example/tickets/FT-3319/attachment/veridian_usage_jul.csv (internal). Timeline note: key created 2026-06-25 14:09 UTC by clare.veridian@veridian.example via console; heavy usage begins 2026-07-04 01:10 UTC; keys disabled 2026-07-04 04:20 UTC.
Priya (Payments): I'll include IP geo lookups showing 185.62.9.10 -> Netherlands VPN provider and 18.197.12.9 -> us-east1. Also include support confirmation that customer denies authorizing the volume.
Theo (CS): Customer asked for provisional refund. Legal prefers we submit evidence first; offer goodwill credit if Stripe rules for customer. I've notified customer we'll keep them updated.
Stripe-Bot: dispute.updated id=dp_1Lz7Yq status=needs_response by=merchant deadline=1715089360
Samira K: Please finalize bundle in 48 hours. Priya, confirm when submitted and paste the Stripe submission id.
Priya (Payments): Submitted evidence via Stripe API. Submission id sb_20260704_09. Waiting for review.
Ben C: Noted one anomalous user-agent string: "redwood-cli/0.9 (bot)" in some calls. Logged in ticket.
Samira K: Thanks all. Keep all artifacts in FT-3319. If Stripe loses dispute, process chargeback and fee; if they rule for us, remove hold after customer confirmation.
